ant_intro_html:
Same pipeline, unchanged code, on the paper's main benchmark: Visual AntMaze (OGBench medium maze, 64×64 pixels from a back camera, 8-D torque actions, success = within 1.0 maze unit of the goal, 350-step budget). Model: pretrained 2-level H-JEPA, seed 42, with the official ant_l2 planner (level-2 GD 90 iterations × 200 samples, level-1 GD 90 × 25, replanning every 10 steps). Test = the official 50 tasks; RASR train (40) and val (20) tasks come from the official grid generator under a different seed, and the code asserts that no start–goal configuration is shared. Env resets are seeded (100000 + task) as on FourRoom.

Unlike FourRoom, failed AntMaze episodes mostly show the ant stalling against a wall or circling near its start, i.e. the low-level controller does not execute the subgoal. That is the case reachability-aware planning is meant for.
ant_p1_html:
Labels as on FourRoom: from every 2nd (train) or 3rd (val/test) planning call of baseline episodes, the simulator state is restored and the frozen level-1 MPC executes the baseline's subgoal for 60 steps with three budgets (B0 2×4, B1 10×20, B2 90×25 = default). A subgoal counts as reached within H ∈ {10, 20, 40, 60} steps if the real level-2 latent comes within eps = 12.06 of it (median latent distance of train frame pairs closer than 0.5 maze units, half the success radius, the same ratio as FourRoom's 8 / 16 px). Restored states are exact (replaying the logged actions from a snapshot reproduces xy with zero error). Renders match to ≤ 1/255 at every call except the first one after reset, where a few isolated pixels differ (task 1: 6 of 4 096 pixels, mean 0.09/255).

The learned predictors do not beat the distance reference here. The logistic on ‖g − z‖² and the controller condition is best on val (AUROC 0.869 vs 0.829 for the MLP) and on test, and it is the one used by the planner (val-selected). The MLP runs are kept as an ablation.
droid_intro_html: DROID in H-JEPA is open-loop planning on recorded real-robot clips: the planner proposes an action sequence from the first frame and a goal frame, and the official metric compares it to the expert's actions (Fréchet fidelity = 1 − F(plan, expert) / F(zero motion, expert)). Nothing can be executed, so this is not a closed-loop test and there is no success rate and no local repair. What can be checked is the P1 + P2 part: whether a reachability score over the level-2 candidate subgoals changes the selected plan, and whether that improves fidelity.
droid_p1_html: Without a controller, the label comes from the expert video: the j-th level-2 subgoal of a candidate plan (level-2 stride 3 frames, 0.6 s) is labelled reachable if it comes within eps of a real expert frame encoding by the time the plan wants to be there (eps = 14.63, median latent distance of expert frames one level-2 step apart, train clips). Candidate pools: 16 level-2 GD samples per clip on 160 train / 40 val clips from DROID training shards (deterministic 80/20 split by episode) and the 16 evaluation clips as test. As on AntMaze, the distance logistic beats the MLP on val and test, so it is the planner's predictor.
droid_p2_html: The planner's level-2 candidate is chosen by cost − λ · c_min · mean_j log(R_j + δ); λ = 0 is the unmodified planner and reproduces the official eval.py output exactly (Fréchet 0.3809, ATE 0.1584 on planner seed 1). Predictor and λ were selected on 24 val clips only.
droid_after_html:
No effect on DROID. Reranking changes the chosen plan on 30 of 48 test runs, but fidelity is unchanged within noise. The val gain of the selected setting (+0.3 points over λ = 0) was already inside the spread of the other settings.

Why no effect

  • The predictor is not the problem. Within one clip it ranks the candidates by their true label with Spearman 0.74 (MLP 0.66), and candidates do differ (on-path fraction from 0.0–0.2 up to 0.4–1.0 per clip).
  • The offline label mostly means “the subgoal stays near the start”. 90% of positive labels match one of the first three expert frames (first 0.6 s), and the positive rate falls from 74% at the first subgoal to 6% at the last. A plan that barely moves is “on the expert path” under a min-over-frames label, which is why the distance to the current state alone reaches AUROC 0.98.
  • So reranking buys conservatism, which the metric does not reward. On the 30 changed runs, the selected candidate has higher mean R (0.18 → 0.39) and an 8% higher progress cost. Fréchet fidelity is measured relative to zero motion, so a plan that moves less does not score better. The fidelity change is uncorrelated with the gain in R (Spearman 0.07) and with the cost given up (0.06).
  • Little room to choose. The released droid_l2 planner keeps only 4 level-2 candidates per clip (the labels were collected with 16).

A time-aligned label (subgoal j must match an expert frame near 3j, not any earlier frame) would remove the “don't move” shortcut. It was not run.
